description: Verify the structure of DUT's ARP Reply — opcode flips from Request (1) to Reply (2) and the sender/target fields swap roles per RFC 826 §2.4
approach:
[Objective]
This case observes the *Reply itself*, not just whether one was sent. RFC 826 §2.4 says the receiver swaps sender↔target in the response and sets opcode=2. Companion cases ARP_43..47 break each Reply field out individually; ARP_41 is the high-level reply-structure check.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected (opcode=1, target_ip=DUT IP, sender=tester)

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: ARP Reply
      - opcode      == 2   (flipped from 1)
      - sender_mac  == DUT iface MAC   (filled in by the responder — the answer)
      - sender_ip   == DUT IP
      - target_*    == HOST-1-IP / MAC-ADDR1   (echoed from Request's sender_*)

[Pass condition]
DUT emits a well-formed ARP Reply matching the swapped-fields shape.

[Fail condition]
Fail_no_reply — DUT did not respond to the Request at all.

verdicts.Pass: DUT emitted a Reply with opcode=2 and swapped sender/target fields — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_reply: DUT did not respond — basic reply mechanism failed
